resolution: A and B transcribed identical `braille.lines`, verified byte-for-byte against lines 6887-6901 after stripping the 5-character line-number field (the '(Return to Text)' line 6902 excluded as PDF-navigation furniture). Structural disagreement over print.blocks: A ordered them to match PRINT's own mid-sentence interruption (paragraph ending 'agreed that', quote, attribution, paragraph continuing 'defeating Hitler...followed', new paragraph); B ordered them to match the ALREADY-RELOCATED braille (one whole uninterrupted sentence, then quote+attribution, then the new paragraph). Settled by reading the PDF page image directly (braille-formats-2016.pdf, p.238): print genuinely shows the quotation interrupting the sentence between 'agreed that' and 'defeating Hitler', confirming A's account of PRINT's own layout -- which is also the only correct input for `buildModel9` (built from `print` only, per this runner's own rule), since B's structure describes the ALREADY-TRANSCRIBED braille, not the print original. Kept A's block order; added the print's own quotation marks (visible in the PDF image but omitted from A's `text`) around the quote, matching B.
